# KindScreen

> Parent-curated catalog of safe YouTube videos for children aged 3–12.

KindScreen is an open source platform where real parents watch and approve YouTube videos before they enter a catalog available to families. No algorithm decides what's safe — only humans do. Every video requires 3 independent parent approvals. One flag from any visitor can trigger moderator review.

## Founder

Built by Felipe Amarante ([@felipeamarante](https://github.com/felipeamarante)) after YouTube Kids exposed his daughter to inappropriate content. The premise: instead of trying to block bad content, only allow verified good content.

## How it works

- **Browse** — anonymous visitors browse the catalog by age band and category. Videos play embedded with YouTube's recommendation engine disabled.
- **Submit** — registered reviewers submit YouTube URLs.
- **Review** — reviewers answer 5 safety questions (blind review — no one sees others' verdicts until they submit). 3 approvals → video enters catalog.
- **Flag** — any visitor can flag an approved video. 3 flags → suspended for moderator review.

## User roles

- Anonymous visitor: browse, watch, flag
- Reviewer: submit videos, review others' submissions
- Trusted Reviewer: same as reviewer, approval counts as 1.5 votes
- Moderator: override decisions, remove/restore videos, manage reviewers
- Admin: full access

## Tech stack

- Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v3
- Supabase (PostgreSQL + Row-Level Security + Auth)
- Hosted on Vercel
- YouTube Data API v3 for video metadata

## Key links

- [GitHub](https://github.com/kindscreenorg/kindscreen): full source code, open source under MIT
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/kindscreenorg/kindscreen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to contribute as a reviewer or developer
- [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/felipeamarante): how the project is funded

## Principles

- Safety first — when in doubt, reject or rate for an older age band
- No VC, no ads, no tracking — community funded
- Built in public — all code and decisions are open
- Humans in the loop — AI may assist, parents always decide
